title: Defining the necessary safety functions of the machine control system in accordance with the risk analysis and ISO 13849-1
description: W skrócie: robimy to, aby maszyna była w pełni bezpieczna dla operatorów. Eliminujemy domysły – opieramy się na precyzyjnych wyliczeniach, tworząc systemy…

blocks.text: Why do we define safety functions?

items: Reducing risk to an acceptable level: Risk analysis identifies hazards, and safety functions (e.g., emergency stop, light curtains) are designed to minimise the risk of accidents.

Compliance with legal and regulatory requirements: This is an essential step towards obtaining CE certification. ISO 13849-1 is harmonised with the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC, which means that its application implies compliance with legal requirements.

Avoiding excessive or insufficient safeguards: Defining the necessary functions allows appropriate measures to be applied – not too weak (which risks an accident) and not too expensive/complex (which generates unnecessary costs), but exactly those resulting from the risk analysis.

Ensuring functionality in the event of a failure: This process defines how the system should behave in the event of a fault, ensuring that the machine enters a safe state rather than, for example, starting up unexpectedly.

blocks.text: How do we design and verify SRP/CS systems?

items: Determining the required PLr (Performance Level required): The standard enables the determination of how reliable a safety function (e.g. emergency stop, light curtain) must be, assigning it a required performance level from ‘a ’ (low) to ‘e’ (high).
Designing reliable systems (SRP/CS): Defining the function allows the safety-related parts of the control system (SRP/CS) to be designed to be fault-tolerant (e.g. redundancy, diagnostics).

Validation and verification: Defining safety functions forms the basis for checking whether the components used (hardware and software) actually achieve the specified PL level, which is essential for machine certification.
Full versatility: This process applies to all technologies (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic) and is essential to ensure that machines operate safely without posing a risk to operators.

blocks.text: Projektowanie oparte na realnych danych

W skrócie: robimy to, aby maszyna była w pełni bezpieczna dla operatorów. Eliminujemy domysły – opieramy się na precyzyjnych wyliczeniach, tworząc systemy sterowania, które ratują życie i zdrowie w ułamku sekundy.
Identification and classification of work
The employer is obliged to identify particularly hazardous work and draw up a list of such tasks. The most common examples are:
Construction and assembly work
Construction, demolition and assembly work is carried out without halting operations at the workplace.
Confined spaces
Work in tanks, sewers, inside technical equipment and in hazardous confined spaces.
Work at height
Work performed on scaffolding, ladders, mobile elevating work platforms or roofs.
Hazardous materials
Activities requiring contact with chemical, toxic, corrosive or flammable substances.
Prace Budowlane i Montażowe
Roboty budowlane, rozbiórkowe i montażowe prowadzone bez wstrzymania ruchu zakładu pracy.
Przestrzenie Zamknięte
Prace w zbiornikach, kanałach, wnętrzach urządzeń technicznych i w niebezpiecznych przestrzeniach zamkniętych.
Prace na Wysokości
Prace wykonywane na rusztowaniach, drabinach, podestach ruchomych czy dachach.
Materiały Niebezpieczne
Czynności wymagające kontaktu z substancjami chemicznymi, toksycznymi, żrącymi lub łatwopalnymi.
Preparation of instructions (IBWR – Instructions for the Safe Performance of Works)
These instructions usually take the form of Safety Work Instructions (IBWR), which the contractor draws up.

items: PURPOSE: To define the rules for organising, carrying out and documenting the work.
SUBJECT AND SCOPE: A detailed description of the work concerned (e.g. ‘welding inside tank X’).
ACTIVITIES BEFORE COMMENCEMENT: Verification of qualifications, medical examinations, site preparation, and provision of collective and personal protective equipment (PPE).
SAFETY PROCEDURES: Sequence of tasks, working techniques, and allocation of tasks by name.
POST-COMPLETION ACTIVITIES: Tidying up the site, handing over equipment, and closing out the work.
EMERGENCY SITUATIONS: Procedures to follow in the event of an accident, fire, or other emergency.

blocks.text: Organisational and formal requirements
The instructions must ensure:
Direct supervision
Appointment of a person to supervise the work.
Written instruction (permit)
Completion of a work permit containing a Job Safety Analysis (JSA).
Staff briefing
Familiarising staff with the IBWR, assigning tasks by name and the sequence of operations.
Site security
Marking and fencing off the work area.
What should the documentation contain?
In addition to the instructions themselves, the documentation package should include:

items: A permit for particularly hazardous work (written instruction).
An occupational risk assessment (often a JSA).
A list of employees with their signatures confirming that they have read the instructions.

blocks.text: The instructions must be understandable to contractors and available on-site.
